name: TX-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about 13 points Republican, and the seat stays open but on the GOP side of the ballot
Steinmann has raised $2.4M with $1.7M in outside support versus roughly $31K for Jones
Polymarket prices Republican odds near 95 percent
No public general-election polling; open-seat status adds mild uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's 13-point Republican lean, Steinmann's roughly 80-to-1 fundraising advantage backed by $1.7 million in outside spending, and market pricing near 95 percent Republican all point the same way, and no polling suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside money or an unexpected open-seat twist could narrow what is otherwise a wide Republican edge.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-08 is a strongly Republican district, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward the GOP. Morgan Luttrell's retirement leaves an open seat, but the Republican advantage remains large. Jessica Hart Steinmann has raised about $2.4 million and drawn roughly $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised about $31,000 with no reported outside spending. Prediction markets put Republican odds near 95 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. The district's lean, the fundraising gap, and market pricing all align in the same direction. A midterm environment that typically favors the out-of-power party would need to be historically strong to put this seat in play. Republicans are positioned to win by a wide margin, with modest uncertainty from the open-seat nature of the contest.
